title: Cheesy Beef Nacho Bake
seoTitle: Cheesy Beef Nacho Bake | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Layered chip bake with seasoned beef and queso for ten
subtitle: Layered chip bake with seasoned beef and queso for ten
description: Tortilla chips are layered with seasoned ground beef, black beans, jalapeños, and two cheeses, then baked until everything melts into a scoopable nacho casserole. Top with sour cream, salsa, and cilantro at the line.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Cheesy Beef Nacho Bake in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch beef. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Brown the beef
steps.instruction: Cook ground beef in a large skillet over medium-high heat, breaking into crumbles until no pink remains. Drain excess fat, stir in taco seasoning and 0.25 cup water until coated.

steps.title: Prep the baking pan
steps.instruction: Lightly grease a large sheet pan or 9x13 dish. Spread half the chips in an even layer, then half the beef, beans, jalapeños, and cheeses.

steps.title: Layer and repeat
steps.instruction: Repeat layers with remaining chips, beef, beans, jalapeños, and cheese. Press gently so layers contact each other and melt into one cohesive bake.

steps.title: Bake until melted
steps.instruction: Bake at 375°F for 18–22 minutes until cheese bubbles at edges and center reaches 165°F where beef is exposed. Rest 5 minutes before topping. Target oven/smoker temperature: 375°F.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 145°F for medium beef, 160°F for ground. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Garnish and serve
steps.instruction: Dollop salsa and sour cream over the hot bake and scatter cilantro. Serve with extra chips on the side for scooping the cheesy bottom layer.

proTips: Add a thin layer of queso between chip layers for extra hold if the crew loves maximum cheese.
Drain beans thoroughly—wet beans steam chips into mush during baking.
Cut into squares for plate service or leave whole for communal scooping.
tonightSpread: Hot nacho bake with salsa, sour cream, guacamole, and lime wedges.
Jalapeño poppers or pickled veggies for crews who want extra heat on the side.
leftovers: Reheat covered at 325°F with a splash of broth to loosen cheese.
Press cold leftovers into a pan and griddle into nacho patty melts.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Traditional nachos get soggy in the middle—this bake solves that with even cheese distribution. One pan feeds ten hungry people and stays hot longer than plated nachos.
mealPrepNotes: Brown beef with taco seasoning ahead and refrigerate. Assemble bake up to 2 hours before oven time. Hold finished bake at 170°F with foil if kickoff delays.
